statement: Appendix is an unedited research-subagent report (snapshot 2026-08-29) tagging claims as [DOC] primary source, [INF] inference, or unverified; versions/dates checked on the snapshot day. Version-sensitive facts will go stale.
research_needed: Re-verify time-sensitive version/status facts before citing them in normative Entrybound documents.

statement: Independent 8-algorithm study (Xeon Gold 6154, ~10 GiB corpora) single-core throughput: Rabin 202 MiB/s at 2 KiB (~13 instructions/byte), Gear 599 MiB/s, Gear64+ SIMD 941 MiB/s.
research_needed: Reproduce CDC throughput on Entrybound target hardware and corpora with the chosen chunker implementation.

statement: AE (hashless extremum) reaches 734 MiB/s with the lowest chunk-size variance; RAM reaches 887 MiB/s but is pathological on low-entropy data.
FastCDC (Gear + normalized chunking + cut-point skip) measured ~2 GB/s by Waterloo and described as the de-facto industry default.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound's chunker throughput against this reference.

statement: SeqCDC (hashless, monotonic byte runs; Middleware '24) measured 4.0-4.25 GB/s at 8 KiB and 8.0-8.8 GB/s at 16 KiB targets.
VectorCDC VRAM (SIMD RAM, FAST '25 / ACM TOS 2026) reaches 29.9 GB/s at 8 KiB with AVX-512 vs FastCDC ~2 GB/s and Rabin ~0.14 GB/s; covers SSE-128, AVX-256, AVX-512, NEON-128, VSX-128.
research_needed: Evaluate a hashless vectorised chunker as a future (versioned) chunker option.
decision_needed: Should a future chunker version adopt a hashless SIMD algorithm?

statement: 2024-2026 throughput frontier moved off hash-based CDC: hashless algorithms (AE, RAM, MAXP) vectorise well; rolling hashes have serial data dependency that defeats SIMD.

VectorCDC claims byte-identical chunk boundaries to the scalar algorithm, hence zero dedup loss. For a deterministic format any SIMD chunker path must yield boundaries identical to the scalar reference across ISAs.
research_needed: Differential test SIMD vs scalar chunker boundaries across x86/ARM/POWER ISAs on adversarial and low-entropy corpora.
decision_needed: Must Entrybound mandate a scalar reference chunker with conformance vectors that every accelerated path must match?

statement: Normalized chunking uses two masks: more one-bits before the expected size, fewer after. Levels NC-1=(14,12), NC-2=(15,11), NC-3=(16,10) one-bits (FastCDC TPDS 2020).
evidence_in_source: primary citation [DOC] Xia et al. TPDS 2020

statement: FastCDC reference configuration is 8 KB average, 2 KB minimum, 64 KB maximum; NC-2 with a 6-8 KB minimum is called the optimal balance.
research_needed: Measure dedup/variance for Entrybound's own min/avg/max choice rather than inheriting research-benchmark sizes.

statement: FastCDC 'rolling two bytes' (fp<<2 with even/odd tables) gives 40-50% additional speed with identical chunking results.
research_needed: If adopted, verify boundary identity against the one-byte reference.

statement: Cut-point skipping yields speedup roughly min/avg but significantly decreases dedup ratio because skipped regions are not content-defined.
research_needed: Quantify dedup loss from Entrybound's minimum chunk size on representative corpora.
decision_needed: What minimum chunk size (skip) does Entrybound accept given dedup loss?

statement: Independent study on Gear: NC-1 ~34% variance reduction, NC-2 ~60% variance reduction for under 2% dedup loss, NC-3 ~75%.
Study's headline recommendation: Gear + NC-2 is the best general-purpose scalar CDC; AE where variance minimisation dominates.
research_needed: Confirm on Entrybound corpora.
decision_needed: Which CDC algorithm and NC level is frozen for Entrybound chunker version 1?

statement: Widely copied AE parameter formula h=mu/(e-1) is wrong, producing chunks 13-39% smaller than target; error propagated into Destor, DedupBench and comparison papers. Corrected approximation h ~ mu-256 for targets >=2 KiB.
refines_or_supersedes: Contradicts/corrects AE formula in Destor, DedupBench and prior comparison papers
research_needed: If AE is used, validate realised average chunk size against target.

statement: RAM chunking fails catastrophically on low-entropy data: source-code corpus produced megabyte-scale chunks with sigma above 12,000 bytes.
research_needed: Include low-entropy corpora in chunker conformance/perf tests.

statement: BFBC's published superiority over Rabin did not reproduce in the independent study.

RapidCDC and QuickCDC memoise previously seen chunk lengths (QuickCDC also 3-byte front/end feature vectors) to fast-forward; reported ~33x over Rabin and 11.4x over RapidCDC, paying off only on duplicate-heavy workloads.

QuickCDC feature-vector matching can accept a chunk whose middle bytes differ, a silent-corruption hazard; source recommends never using QuickCDC-style acceptance in a durability-critical format. Dedup matches must be decided on full content identity.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound dedup path to confirm matches require full digest equality over all bytes.

statement: Chonkers (arXiv:2509.11121, Sept 2025) is the first CDC with provable strict guarantees on chunk size and edit locality; measured locality average below 1, max <=5; no throughput numbers and deliberately unoptimised reference; not yet production candidate.
research_needed: Track optimised implementations and benchmarks.

statement: Anchor-based CDC like FastCDC cannot prevent boundary shifts arbitrarily far after local edits; edit-locality or dedup-stability claims made for such chunkers are not provably bounded.
research_needed: Measure boundary resynchronisation distance after edits for Entrybound's chunker; avoid unbounded locality claims.

statement: restic chunker: min 512 KiB / avg ~1 MiB / max 8 MiB, 64-byte window, splitmask (1<<20)-1.
BorgBackup default chunker params: min 512 KiB / avg ~2 MiB / max 8 MiB (19,23,21,...).
Kopia targets 4 MiB chunks by default (DYNAMIC-4M-BUZHASH), offering 128K-8M.
Duplicacy chunk sizes: min 1 MB / avg 4 MB / max 16 MB.
casync/desync: buzhash 48-byte window, min 16 KB / avg 64 KB / max 256 KB; recommended ratio min=avg/4, max=4x avg.
bup: avg 8 KiB, max 4x avg (32 KiB), rollsum 64-byte window, 13 zero bits trigger a boundary.
zpaq default -fragment 6 gives ~64 KiB average fragments; -fragment N spans 64*2^N to 8128*2^N bytes; costs ~28 bytes archive and 40 bytes RAM per fragment.
Duplicati uses 100 KB fixed blocks and 50 MB volumes.
Nydus RAFS uses 1 MB fixed chunks, each with a SHA-256 block_id, enabling cross-inode, cross-layer and cross-image dedup.
IPFS UnixFS recommends 256 KiB (legacy) or 1 MiB (modern maximum recommended) blocks (spec draft 22 Aug 2026).
MSIX/AppX uses 64 KB fixed blocks with one SHA2-256 hash per block.
Pattern: backup tools shipping a chunk index to every client choose MiB-scale chunks; HTTP content-distribution tools 64 KiB-1 MiB; research benchmarks 2-16 KiB.
research_needed: Choose Entrybound chunk sizes from its own index-cost vs dedup vs range-fetch measurements.
decision_needed: What CDC min/avg/max does Entrybound freeze, and is it profile-dependent?

statement: Borg measured on 37 GB VM data: 64 KiB avg -> 378,374 chunks, 20 MB index, 14.81 GB stored; 1 MiB -> 25,889 chunks, 1.3 MB index, 14.60 GB; 8 MiB -> 4,319 chunks, 327 KB index, 14.59 GB.
evidence_in_source: primary citation [DOC] measured by Borg project

statement: Borg RAM use is about 2.1x the repository index size; on VM images compressed size barely changed with chunk size, so index cost dominates dedup gain beyond ~1 MiB.
evidence_in_source: primary citation [DOC] + author inference on VM data
research_needed: Measure Entrybound index size and reader RAM vs chunk size on VM-image and many-small-file corpora.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound bound index RAM independent of archive size (e.g. paged index)?

statement: Two independent 2025 papers broke seed-randomised CDC; source calls this the most consequential development for a new encrypted archive format.
Alexeev/Percival/Zhang (Mar 2025) threat model: attacker is the storage server seeing only encrypted chunk sizes.
research_needed: Decide whether Entrybound's threat model includes an observer of ciphertext unit sizes (storage host, network).

statement: Attack costs: Tarsnap chosen-plaintext 2^42 (prime, multiplier, map); Borg uncompressed known-plaintext 2^21*k (32-bit Buzhash table); Borg compressed chosen-plaintext 2^42; restic known-plaintext 2^44*k (degree-53 polynomial).

After chunker-secret recovery the server can fingerprint known files from chunk-size sequences (two sizes identified songs), infer ~20% of low-entropy genomic content, and extract targeted secrets with ~2^21 adversarial prefix/suffix bytes per bit.
Recommended fixes: Tarsnap secondary rolling hash and larger prime; Borg widen Buzhash 32->256 bits and require compression; restic double polynomial degree to ~128.
Paper stresses compression as default, or even required, is important against chunk-size attacks. Implication: encrypted chunked archives should not store chunks uncompressed by default.
research_needed: Quantify how much compression alone reduces chunk-size fingerprinting for Entrybound's units.
decision_needed: Must compression be mandatory (or default) for encrypted Entrybound archives?

statement: Truong/Merz/Scarlata/Guenther/Paterson (ACM CCS 2025): seed-based randomisation of chunk boundaries is not secure generically.
Countermeasure 1: pad every chunk to maximum size, which mitigates but carries no formal guarantee.
research_needed: Measure storage overhead and residual leakage of Entrybound's padding schedule.

statement: Countermeasure 2: encrypt the rolling hash with AES before the threshold comparison; provably secure, costing ~50-160% chunking overhead, partially absorbed by AES-NI.
research_needed: Benchmark AES-in-the-loop CDC throughput on Entrybound targets with/without AES-NI.

research_needed: Read the full paper (ePrint 2025/558 / DOI 10.1145/3719027.3744870) before freezing CDC-leakage countermeasures.

research_needed: Determine technical content of restic 0.18.0 mitigation.

statement: Borg declined to change its chunker because it would break dedup on existing repos (potentially doubling storage); it points to its obfuscate pseudo-compressor (since 1.2.0) that randomly pads stored chunk sizes at no dedup cost since IDs are over plaintext.

research_needed: Leakage analysis and overhead measurement for each option under Entrybound's unit layout.

statement: A chunker is not upgradable in place once repositories are deployed (Borg lesson); version and negotiate the chunking algorithm and parameters from day one.
research_needed: Verify that chunker identity/version and parameters are recorded in the format and that readers never depend on them for decode.

statement: restic (stable 0.19.1, 2026-07-05) chunks with Rabin, 64-byte window, using a random irreducible polynomial per repository stored in config to hinder watermark attacks; §1.7 shows the polynomial is recoverable.
refines_or_supersedes: Refined within source by §1.7 L91 (polynomial recoverable)

statement: restic pack format: encrypted blobs, then encrypted header, then 4-byte LE header length; header lists per-blob type, encrypted length, plaintext hash, and uncompressed length for compressed blobs.
restic's key architectural win: each blob independently encrypted and authenticated, so readers fetch the trailing header then range-read one blob, and repacking never touches blob ciphertexts.
research_needed: Check whether Entrybound units are independently authenticated so repack can move ciphertext without re-encryption.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound repack preserve encrypted unit ciphertexts verbatim?

statement: restic index is JSON pack-to-blob maps (offset/length/hash) kept under 8 MiB per index file with a supersedes field for repack; default pack size 16 MiB, tunable via --pack-size.
restic crypto: AES-256-CTR + Poly1305-AES, keys via scrypt; 16-byte IV + ciphertext + 16-byte MAC per blob.

restic's flat in-RAM chunk index is a long-standing scaling pain (issue #2523 since 2019; 0.19.0 fixes still target index memory); source calls it the most persistent architectural mistake in the category. A format should not require loading a whole flat chunk index into RAM.
evidence_in_source: primary citation [DOC] issues/release notes + author judgement
research_needed: Measure Entrybound reader/writer peak memory vs chunk count at large scale (e.g. 10^8 chunks).
decision_needed: Must Entrybound's index be pageable/partially loadable with bounded RAM?

statement: Borg stable is 1.4.4 (2026-03-19); Borg 2.0 remains beta (2.0.0b21, 2026-03-15), labelled testing-only and not for production repositories after years in beta.

Borg 2.0 repository model abandons transactional append-only segments for separate objects with no refcounting and garbage collection over the borgstore KV abstraction (file, sftp, rclone, s3/b2, REST); most operations become concurrency-safe.
Borg 2.0 moves the chunk index into the repository so all clients share it, removing expensive per-client resync (the class of problem restic still has).
Borg 2.0 makes fastcdc the default alongside improved buzhash64, SIMD on x86-64 and ARM64, plus fingerprinting-resistant variants.
Borg 2.0 crypto: AEAD (AES-OCB, ChaCha20-Poly1305), Argon2, session keys to eliminate long-term nonce/counter management, BLAKE3 replacing BLAKE2b.
Borg keyed chunk IDs: MAC over plaintext under secret id_key (HMAC-SHA256 or keyed BLAKE3) prevents matching hashes of known small files and chunk-ID prediction; orthogonal to the chunk-size leak.
research_needed: Assess whether unkeyed plaintext digests exposed in Entrybound encrypted archives enable known-file confirmation.
decision_needed: Are chunk/content digests visible to non-key-holders in encrypted Entrybound archives, and must they be keyed?

statement: Borg 2.0 adds soft delete plus borg compact and borg undelete.
Kopia (0.23.0, 2026-05-12) splitters: FIXED-{128K..8M}, DYNAMIC-{128K..8M}-BUZHASH, DYNAMIC-{128K..8M}-RABINKARP; default DYNAMIC-4M-BUZHASH.

Kopia packs content-addressable blocks (<=20 MB) into 20-40 MB pack blobs with randomised names so filenames leak nothing; ciphers AES256-GCM-HMAC-SHA256 and CHACHA20-POLY1305-HMAC-SHA256; hashes SHA-2/BLAKE2s.

Kopia epoch index manager: append-only repository for ransomware/object-lock; epoch-prefixed index blobs, clients agree within +-1 epoch, deterministic merge into identical compacted blobs, range compaction; trades point-in-time granularity for not scanning all indexes. Index bloat still reported (#5057).
Kopia v0.23.0 removed LZ4 compression support, a breaking change: codec removal can strand existing data.
research_needed: Define Entrybound codec deprecation policy that never removes decode support for published archives.
decision_needed: What is Entrybound's policy for deprecating codecs while keeping old archives decodable?

statement: Duplicacy keeps no chunk index: chunks are individual objects named by content hash and existence is tested via the storage API, making minimal cloud storage a backup backend.

Duplicacy two-step fossil collection enables lock-free GC: unreferenced chunks are renamed to fossils and deleted only after every snapshot ID has a newer snapshot created and finished after collection.

Duplicacy pack-and-split conceptually concatenates files in alphabetical order before splitting so renames and reorganisation dedup well; setting fixed chunking disables it and chunks per file, suited to VM/DB images.
research_needed: Measure rename/move dedup for per-file vs cross-file chunking on Entrybound corpora.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound chunk per entry or across a concatenated ordered stream?

statement: Duplicacy uses four 256-bit keys under a PBKDF2 master key: chunk hash is HMAC-SHA256 under hash key, exposed filename derived from hash under ID key, per-chunk AES-GCM key = HMAC(chunk hash, chunk key).
Cost of Duplicacy's no-index design: one object per chunk is fine on S3 but brutal on FTP/WebDAV and filesystems with per-file overhead.

bup hashsplit tree: extra rollsum bits beyond the 13 boundary bits define higher-level split points, forming a content-defined tree; edits change O(log n) objects and the tree is stable under insertion. Flat chunk list overhead ~0.25%.
research_needed: Evaluate content-defined index trees for Entrybound incremental/diff index stability.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound's chunk list/index for large entries be a content-defined tree rather than a flat list?

statement: bup writes git packfiles directly and added midx multi-index files plus bloom filters because a 200 GB dataset across 200 packfiles needed ~600-800 memory pages per object lookup; bupindex is a separate shareable metadata cache.

casync: catar is a reproducible random-accessible tar; .caibx/.caidx hold chunk index (offset + hash list); .castr chunk store; chunk IDs are SHA512-256 of uncompressed data, stored zstd-compressed as .cacnk.
casync removes file boundaries before chunking to find cross-file similarity that per-file chunkers miss, and --seed reconstructs from local data, fetching only the delta.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound support seeding extraction/fetch from locally available chunks?

statement: casync upstream is dormant (2 releases, latest v2 2017-07-26) while desync is live; lesson: the format outlived the tool because it was simple and documented. Formats should be simple and independently documented.
research_needed: Build an independent minimal reader from the spec alone to validate documentation sufficiency.

statement: Duplicati uses fixed 100 KB blocks (min 10 KB), 50 MB dblock volumes, and block size cannot change after initial backup; one-byte change rewrites a block, one-file extract downloads a 50 MB volume, corruption destroys a volume, SQLite lookup grows unboundedly.
Fixed-size blocks give up insertion resilience for nothing that CDC with a minimum-size floor cannot provide.
Never make a chunking parameter permanently unchangeable.
research_needed: Verify chunk parameters are per-archive/per-unit metadata, not global format constants.

statement: A volume that cannot be range-read is a solid archive by another name; storage units must be range-addressable.

NAR has three node types, stores only type, executable bit, length-prefixed contents, symlink target and names; omits uid/gid, other permissions, timestamps, xattrs, ACLs; directory entries sorted by name; bit-for-bit reproducible because NAR hash is store path identity.
research_needed: Use as input for a NAR import/export adapter fidelity matrix.

statement: NAR's documented cost is no random access and no index (locating a file deserialises everything before it); binary caches compress whole NARs (xz historically, zstd now) with a .narinfo sidecar.
Reproducibility and seekability are separable concerns and a format can have both; NAR merely chose not to.
research_needed: Demonstrate Entrybound byte-identical reproducible output with indexed layout.

statement: OSTree (v2026.2) repo modes archive, bare, bare-user, bare-split-xattrs; archive mode gzips each content object individually with uncompressed metadata, servable from plain HTTP/CDN.

Naive content-addressing over HTTP fails with one request per changed file; OSTree static deltas precompute commit-to-commit deltas (superblock, per-part sizes, fallback objects, bsdiff for same-basename files) spending server storage to save client bandwidth.
research_needed: Measure request counts for Entrybound remote partial fetch with many small entries; consider range coalescing.

statement: Since v2025.1 OSTree always generates a composefs blob at deployment, but composefs integration is still marked experimental, not for production.

Git pack idx v2: magic, 256-entry fanout, sorted OID table, CRC32 per object (copy between packs without re-verifying), 31-bit offsets with MSB flag into 64-bit large-offset table; .rev reverse index; MIDX with chunked PNAM/OIDF/OIDL/OOFF/LOFF/RIDX sections.

Git deltas OBJ_OFS_DELTA/OBJ_REF_DELTA; defaults --window 10, --depth 50, max depth 4095; man page warns deep chains slow unpacking. Source calls this the delta-chain analogue of the solid-archive penalty, hence capped depth.
Dependency chains (delta depth, lookback) must be capped rather than maximised because reconstruction applies the whole chain serially.
research_needed: Measure ratio vs extract latency across lookback/delta-depth caps on Entrybound corpora.
decision_needed: What maximum lookback/dependency depth does Entrybound declare and enforce?

statement: Seekable zstd layout: N independent zstd frames then a skippable frame (magic 0x184D2A5E) holding 8-byte seek entries (compressed/decompressed size, optional 4-byte checksum) and a 9-byte footer (frame count, descriptor bit7 checksum flag, magic 0x8F92EAB1).
Seekable zstd hard limits: max 134,217,728 frames, max 1 GiB decompressed per frame, default max frame size 2 GB when unspecified.
Seekable zstd index overhead is 8 bytes per frame plus 13 fixed (12 with checksums); 1 GiB at 64 KiB frames gives 16,384 entries, ~128 KB, ~0.012%.
zstd seekable README: choose frame size about equal to access granularity; avoid frames under 1 KB due to large compression-ratio loss.
research_needed: Measure ratio loss for Entrybound's smallest independent units.

statement: Seekable zstd lives in contrib/, is not part of the core zstd specification, and the README makes no stability or standardisation claim; depending on it carries format-stability risk.
research_needed: Confirm whether Entrybound depends on any contrib/non-normative zstd layout.

statement: zeekstd (Rust, spec v0.1.1 2025-02-05) deprecates seek-table checksums in favour of frame content checksums and adds a forward-readable Head seek-table variant incompatible with older decoders: cost of leaving a format unversioned in contrib.
Formats must carry explicit versioning so extensions (e.g. head vs foot index placement, checksum changes) do not silently fork and break older decoders.

WARC/1.1 zstd (IIPC, proposed): one zstd frame per record with mandatory Frame_Content_Size and Content_Checksum, optional shared dictionary frame at file head, no built-in seek table (external index needed). sqlitezstd is a SQLite VFS over seekable zstd.

zstd:chunked extends OCI tar+zstd with per-file and per-chunk zstd compression, TOC in skippable frames (magic 0x184D2A50), and a 64-byte footer of eight LE u64 (manifest offset/lengths/type, tar-split offset/lengths, magic GNUlInUx).

zstd:chunked TOC entries carry type, name, linkname, mode, size, uid/gid, three timestamps, device numbers, xattrs, content digest, offsets, and per-chunk size/offset/digest; a 'zeros' chunk type makes sparse regions cost nothing.

zstd:chunked runtime keeps an mmap-able manifest cache of file and chunk sha256, hardlinks or reflinks matching files from existing layers on pull, applies fsverity if configured; partial pulls gated behind enable_partial_images.
zstd:chunked is not officially standardized or documented beyond reference-implementation code (manpage admission).

zstd:chunked silently downgrades to plain zstd when images are encrypted, so seekability is lost under encryption; tracking checklist shows remaining items are making zstd default and blob-cache mixing.
research_needed: Verify Entrybound encrypted archives retain indexed random access and that no feature silently downgrades.
decision_needed: Must Entrybound refuse (rather than silently drop) features that cannot compose with encryption?

location: §3 zstd:chunked L226; What I could not verify L431
statement: Whether zstd:chunked splits files into chunks by content-defined or fixed chunking is undocumented; manpage and PR defer to source code. Unverified.
research_needed: Read containers/storage source to determine chunking method.

statement: eStargz (stargz-snapshotter v0.18.2, 2025-01-21) is a valid gzip tar with forced gzip member boundaries at blob top, each non-empty regular file payload, TOC header, and footer; large files split across members.

eStargz TOC is stargz.index.json as the last tar entry; TOCEntry fields include name, type (dir/reg/symlink/hardlink/char/block/fifo/chunk), mode, uid, gid, size, digest, chunkDigest, offsets, chunkSize, innerOffset, linkName, modtime, user/group names, dev numbers, xattrs.

eStargz footer is exactly 51 bytes (gzip header with SG extra subfield encoding hex TOC offset + STARGZ, empty final block, gzip trailer); client range-GETs last 51 bytes, then the TOC, then individual chunks.
Verifiable eStargz: manifest annotation toc.digest covers the whole TOC JSON and each reg/chunk entry's chunkDigest covers its bytes, forming a manifest -> TOC -> chunk verification chain.
eStargz prefetch landmarks (.prefetch.landmark / .no.prefetch.landmark tar entries) separate startup-needed files from the rest so runtimes fetch one contiguous hot range.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound layout support declared hot-set ordering for remote prefetch?

statement: eStargz external-TOC variant uses footer magic STARGZEXTERNALTOC with TOC in a separate image linked by layer.digest; per-file gzip header overhead is managed by --estargz-min-chunk-size coalescing small files addressed via innerOffset.
eStargz standardisation remains open: OCI image-spec issue #815 and PR #877 open; no TOC/lazy-pull annotation exists in current OCI annotations spec.

SOCI leaves OCI images byte-identical and ships a separate artifact: index manifest referencing one zTOC per layer (file-to-decompressed-offset TOC plus zlib decompressor checkpoints); spans independently decompressible, fetched by ranged GET with local caching.
research_needed: Assess checkpoint-index approach for random access into legacy gzip/tar sources.

statement: SOCI default indexing threshold is 10 MB minimum layer size; AWS says images over 250 MB benefit most and for small images lazy-loading overhead can exceed a full pull.

statement: SOCI v1 linked index to image via OCI subject/referrers; replication tooling missed the index and index changes mid-deployment caused inconsistent lazy/non-lazy tasks; v2 (2025-07-03) wraps both in an image index with explicit digest annotations, needing soci-snapshotter v0.10.0+.
A loosely coupled sidecar index will be separated from its data by tooling unaware of it; bind any index/sidecar to content by a mechanism the ecosystem's copy tools already respect.

statement: squashfs: 96-byte superblock (magic 0x73717368) with six tables; data blocks 4 KiB-1 MiB power of two (default 128 KiB); metadata blocks fixed 8 KiB with 16-bit header; tail-ends packed into fragment blocks; block location = blocks_start + sum of previous sizes.
squashfs uses one compressor for the whole archive and limits: at most 2^16 unique UID/GIDs, 256-character names, basic file inodes capped at 4 GiB.
research_needed: Feed limits into squashfs import/export fidelity matrix.

statement: EROFS compresses into fixed-size output physical clusters rather than fixed input, gaining ~5% space at 4-8 KiB pclusters; pclusters cache independently, can be referenced multiple times for dedup, and support in-place decompression.

EROFS codecs by kernel: LZ4, MicroLZMA 5.16, DEFLATE 6.6, Zstandard 6.10, QAT DEFLATE 6.16, metadata compression 6.17; file-backed mounts 6.12; dedup via fixed chunks, compressed-cluster dedup with Rabin-Karp adjusted cut points, and fragments/extents.
Android enables EROFS per partition with default compressor lz4hc, ~25% smaller on average and up to 45% at highest levels; no zstd option documented there.

Independent 2026-03-22 benchmark: squashfs zstd smaller (15.8 MB vs EROFS lz4hc 17.1 MB on 50 MB rootfs) but EROFS ~3x random-read IOPS (7,200-8,650 vs 1,920-2,840) because it decompresses at page not block granularity.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound random-read latency vs independent unit size.

statement: DwarFS (0.15.5/0.15.6, July 2026; format v2.5) is described as the most directly relevant existing design to Entrybound.
research_needed: Include DwarFS in incumbent capability comparison and benchmark suite.

statement: DwarFS sections: 8-byte magic+version, SHA-512/256 (32 B) full integrity, XXH3-64 (8 B) fast check, section number/type/compression (4 B each), 8-byte length, payload; no padding; types BLOCK, METADATA_V2_SCHEMA, METADATA_V2, SECTION_INDEX, HISTORY.
DwarFS SECTION_INDEX is optional, must be last, and packs section type in the upper 16 bits and offset in the lower 48 bits per entry.

DwarFS metadata is Frozen2: bit-packed, memory-mappable, with a separate Thrift schema section declaring each field's bit width (unused fields zero bits); inodes strictly ordered by type for binary-search categorisation; tables sorted for reproducibility; optional FSST name compression and delta-packed tables.
research_needed: Compare Entrybound manifest size and open latency vs Frozen2 on million-file trees.

statement: DwarFS categorizer framework: pcmaudio (splits waveform/metadata, FLAC, sample-based windows), incompressible (fast zstd probe, recommended last), binary (ELF/PE/Mach-O by architecture), hotness (from supplied list); compression, order, lookback, window and bloom settings configurable per category.
DwarFS similarity ordering options: fast similarity hash, nilsimsa recursive divide-and-conquer clustering (max-children, max-cluster-size), or explicit file order.

DwarFS segmentation finds identical byte ranges across files with cyclic hashes (window-size log2, window-step) accelerated by a bloom filter; --max-lookback-blocks defaults to 1, the solid-vs-random-access dial trading ratio for larger virtual blocks and latency.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound ChunkGroup lookback settings vs ratio and access latency against DwarFS defaults.

statement: DwarFS recommends --block-size-bits 20-26 (1-64 MiB); levels 8-9 switch to LZMA with ~10x slower access.
DwarFS sparse files (v0.14.0+) represent holes using block index N in an N-block filesystem with chunk.offset = hole_size % BLOCK_SIZE and chunk.size = hole_size / BLOCK_SIZE.

DwarFS README results: 47.49 GiB Perl installs (1.9M files) to 0.310 GiB (153.2:1) in 2m13s vs SquashFS 14.63:1 in 5m37s; 465.2 GiB CI artifacts 16.25:1 vs 7-Zip 7.748:1 with mount 0.024s vs 10.5s; audio 1.664 GiB vs SquashFS 2.711 GiB.
research_needed: Independently reproduce and include DwarFS as baseline before any Entrybound ratio/speed superiority claim.

statement: BGZF is a valid gzip stream of complete RFC1952 members each <=64 KiB with BC extra subfield (block size minus one); virtual offsets pack compressed block offset and in-block offset; fixed 28-byte empty EOF block detects truncation; external .gzi/tabix/CSI indexes.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound legacy export to gzip emit BGZF-style blocked members for seekability?

statement: BGZF proves seekability can be retrofitted into gzip at zero format-compatibility cost, a trick eStargz later generalised.

pixz splits into independent xz blocks for parallel compress and decompress and auto-indexes tarballs for multi-core single-file extraction with index verification; limited to tar indexing, needs liblzma >=4.999.9beta212, .tpxz is pixz-specific.

Sarai's tar critique: tar is a family not a format (five xattr encodings, no canonical form); not parallelizable; not reproducible across implementations/versions; dedup effectively useless (one byte change re-downloads layer); whiteouts are an incompatible hack forbidding .wh. names and making deletion grow images.
research_needed: Use in tar adapter reconciliation and conflict classes (xattr encoding variants).

statement: Source recommends Sarai's seven OCIv2 requirements as a design checklist: machine-independent representation, deduplication, parallelizable operations, sensible deletion, reproducible canonical form, non-avalanching changes, transparency about contents.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound spec against each of the seven items and record gaps.

location: §4 What tar gets wrong L295, L297
statement: Sensible deletion (vs tar whiteouts that increase size and reserve names) is one of the seven checklist items; how an Entrybound incremental/layered archive represents deletions is not addressed here.
research_needed: Check Entrybound incremental/base-chain spec for deletion representation.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound represent entry deletion in incremental archives without reserved names or size growth?

location: §4 How partial retrieval over HTTP works L300-303
statement: All production partial-retrieval designs share three steps: fixed-size self-locating tail (eStargz 51 B, zstd:chunked 64 B, seekable zstd 9 B) for an unconditional first range request; one GET for the TOC; range GETs of independently decompressible ranges.
research_needed: Count round trips for Entrybound remote open and single-entry extract.

statement: SOCI is the exception, placing its index in a separate registry artifact to leave the blob untouched, and paid with the v1->v2 replication-consistency problem.

Nydus separates bootstrap (metadata Merkle tree over the filesystem) from blob data; supports lz4/gzip/zstd/none; a prefetch table carries build-time fetch hints; RAFS v5 FUSE-based, RAFS v6 EROFS-compatible so the kernel does reads.

composefs: EROFS image holds only metadata with overlay redirect xattrs to content-addressed backing files and metacopy fs-verity digests; fs-verity on the EROFS image closes the directory-structure gap; images share page cache and dedup identical files even when timestamps/ownership differ.
fs-verity alone protects file contents but not directory structure; integrity of names/tree must be covered separately (composefs does so by verity over the metadata image).
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound's root digest covers names, tree structure and metadata, not only content.

statement: AWS SOCI Parallel Pull Mode (2025-08-27) added parallel eager download/unpack because AI/ML containers access data immediately; 10 GB DLC with vLLM went from 1m52.876s to 45.121s (~60% faster).

Seekability and parallel bulk transfer are different optimisations; design the index of independent offset-addressable blocks so it serves both single-block fetch and fetching all blocks over N connections.
research_needed: Benchmark Entrybound full extract over N parallel range connections vs sequential.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's index support parallel whole-archive fetch/decode in addition to random access?

statement: Apple Encrypted Archive details come from reverse-engineering (The Apple Wiki, kinnay/AEA); no official Apple specification exists.
research_needed: Treat AEA comparisons as provisional; verify against implementation if cited.

statement: AEA (magic AEA1) identity is SHA-256 of the entire prologue; six profiles: 0 signed only (ECDSA P-256), 1 symmetric, 2 symmetric+signed, 3 ECDHE, 4 ECDHE+signed, 5 scrypt password. Source calls it the best-designed encrypted seekable container found.

AEA prologue: magic, profile ID, scrypt hardness, auth-data length and data, prologue signature (128/160 B), encryption data (32/65 B), salt (32), root HMAC (32), root header (48, encrypted on profiles 1-5), first cluster HMAC (32); minimum 156 bytes for profile 1.
AEA derives all keys with HKDF-SHA256 (main key info 'AEA_AMK' + profile ID), then hierarchically: root header key, cluster key, cluster-header key, segment key.
AEA defaults to 256 segments per cluster and 1 MB per segment; each cluster holds encrypted segment info (sizes + checksum), a next-cluster HMAC, and per-segment HMACs (32 B each).

AEA integrity is an HMAC chain over clusters: random-access decrypts one segment via derived keys, but authenticating cluster N implies having authenticated clusters 0..N-1 (walk cost inferred, not stated by the wiki).
research_needed: Confirm AEA verification walk cost if used in comparisons.

statement: Improve on AEA by replacing the HMAC chain with a Merkle tree so verifying segment N does not require a linear walk; hash chains are cheapest to write but worst for random verification and should be avoided.
research_needed: Verify Entrybound partial verification cost is O(log n) or O(1) per unit, not linear.

statement: What AEA does that ZIP/tar cannot: authenticated encryption with per-segment MACs, ECDSA-signed prologue committing to the whole archive, random-access decryption of a 1 MB segment, per-segment size metadata giving O(1) seek within a cluster.
research_needed: Include AEA in incumbent capability comparison for encrypted random access.

statement: Apple Archive (.aar/.yaa) is LZFSE-centric (also LZ4, LZMA, ZLIB), preserves the full HFS+/APFS attribute set including xattrs, and preserves APFS clone files and sparse files; no official format spec.
Preserving sparse/clone files carries a noted DoS risk: decompression expands them (e.g. 10 GB sparse file occupying 4 MB). Extraction must bound expanded output.
research_needed: Test Entrybound extraction of large sparse/clone entries against declared resource budgets and non-sparse-capable filesystems.
decision_needed: What expansion limit/policy applies when restoring sparse or cloned entries onto filesystems that cannot preserve sparseness?

statement: Zarc: zstd frames with metadata in skippable frames, directory at end, BLAKE3 content-addressed dedup, BLAKE3-verified directory, always-on integrity, xattrs, high-resolution timestamps, archive/file user metadata, minimal overhead.
Zarc's explicit non-goals were encryption, tar/zip compatibility and file splitting; dual Apache-2.0/MIT; repository archived 2025-02-06 and author calls it a toy not for production data.

ZArchive (v0.1.2, 2022-09-08): zstd in 64 KiB blocks with offset table for in-file random reads; file size limit 2^48-1; whole-archive SHA-256; big-endian; write-once and creatable without seeking so it can stream to network or write-once media.
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound writers can produce indexed archives on non-seekable outputs.
decision_needed: Must every Entrybound layout be writable to a non-seekable sink?

statement: RAR5: signature 52 61 72 21 1A 07 01 00; vint headers with CRC32, type, flags, extra area; recovery records; optional BLAKE2sp checksum; AES-256-CBC with PBKDF2 (iteration count as log2), 16-byte salt and IV, 12-byte password check value.

RAR5 quick-open record duplicates headers for listing; spec warns quick-open data used for display must also be used for extraction or displayed and extracted content can disagree. Duplicated listing metadata must never diverge from what extraction uses.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound for any duplicated metadata (index vs manifest vs local headers) and ensure a single authoritative source or mandatory consistency check.

statement: RAR5 'tweaked checksums' become key-dependent under encryption to prevent content guessing from plaintext checksums.
RAR5 dictionary 128 KB-4096 MB; files flagged as depending on preceding file block cannot decompress independently; in solid mode random access is impossible without processing predecessors.
WinRAR docs: extracting one file from a solid archive requires analysing all preceding files, and damage to any file makes all following files unextractable.
research_needed: Measure Entrybound corruption blast radius per ChunkGroup/lookback setting.

statement: 7z: 32-byte signature header (magic, version 0.4, start-header CRC, next-header offset/size/CRC); folders are solid units with up to 5 chained coders (LZMA/LZMA2/COPY/DELTA/BCJ/AES); substreams carve files; one-file extract decompresses whole folder; headers may be encoded/encrypted (0x17).
zpaq has two format types: streaming (single-pass extraction, no dedup, no rollback, backward compatible pre-6.00) and journaling (dedup, rollback, multi-part).

zpaq journaling uses D (data), C/fragment (SHA-1 hashes), H (transaction headers) and I (index) blocks; updates write a temporary header, append data and index, then rewrite the header last so interrupted appends are ignored and overwritten next time.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound support crash-safe append/update, and with what commit protocol?

statement: zpaq's -all exposes every historical version: the archive is a versioned log not a snapshot, allowing rollback to any prior state with appending never rewriting; source lists this as something ZIP/tar cannot do.
decision_needed: Is a versioned/append-log archive mode in or out of scope for Entrybound?

statement: WIM codecs: XPRESS (dict 4-64 KiB), LZX (32 KiB-2 MiB, x86 preprocessing), LZMS (undocumented, up to 64 MiB, solid); chunk sizes LZX/XPRESS 32,768, LZMS non-solid 131,072, LZMS solid 64 MiB; single-instancing across images.

WIM non-solid chunked mode with a chunk table is the compressed-but-seekable design, while solid resources trade seekability for ratio; wimlib LZX 125,929,467 B in 27.5s vs WIMGAPI 127,295,034 B in 45.9s on a WinPE image.

MSIX AppxBlockMap.xml lists per file name, size, local header size and one SHA2-256 per 64 KB block; differential update downloads only mismatched blocks; Microsoft advises keeping changes within 64 KB boundaries and avoiding mid-file modifications.
Fixed-size blocking makes a format's differential-update efficiency the application developer's problem, which is the argument for CDC.
research_needed: Measure differential-update bytes for CDC vs fixed blocks on real app update pairs.

statement: BLAKE3 tree parameters: 1024-byte leaf chunks, 32-byte chaining values, parent nodes compress a 64-byte concatenation of two child CVs.
Bao combined encoding concatenates chunks and parents in pre-order with an 8-byte LE input length prepended, letting the decoder verify each node while streaming.

Bao outboard encoding omits chunks so the decoder reads the original file plus a small tree; source says this is the property an archive wants: verification metadata that does not require rewriting the payload.
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound's Merkle/outboard layout allows adding/rebuilding verification data without rewriting payload.

statement: Bao slice holds only the chunks and parents needed for one byte range; a slice over the whole input is byte-identical to the combined encoding.
In Bao, a length is considered validated when and only when the decoder validates the final chunk; a declared length claim alone is untrustworthy until proven.
research_needed: Audit Entrybound readers so declared sizes are used only as bounded hints until authenticated; fuzz with lying lengths.

statement: Bao overhead is 32 bytes of parent nodes per 1024-byte chunk pair, asymptotically ~1 parent per chunk, ~3.1% for combined encoding (arithmetic inference; spec states no formula).

Bab (2024/2025) redesigns Bao: hash-function-agnostic, short string-length proofs, more efficient slice requests, freely choosable chunk size (WILLIAM3 uses 1024), tree shape matching RFC 9162 (complete left subtrees, strictly decreasing sizes).
A verified-range scheme designed from scratch should start from Bab's critique of Bao.
research_needed: Review Entrybound Merkle layout against Bab's critique (length proofs, slice efficiency, tree shape).

statement: fs-verity: block size defaults to page size (typically 4096), since Linux 6.3 any power of two from 1024 to min(page, fs block); SHA-256 default; ~128 hashes per 4 KiB block giving ~1/127 (~0.79%) overhead.

Never publish a bare Merkle root as identity; publish a hash of a descriptor binding the root to its parameters (version, hash algorithm, log2 block size, salt, file size), as fs-verity does to eliminate file/padding ambiguity.
research_needed: Formal check that Entrybound identity roots bind tree parameters and length; test for collisions across parameter sets.

statement: fs-verity verifies lazily per block on read with cached hash blocks, so sequential reads usually find the bottom-level hash block already verified.

location: §6 dm-verity L387; What I could not verify L433
statement: dm-verity data_block_size and hash_block_size are explicit parameters with no defaults stated in kernel docs; 4096 is conventional but unverified.
research_needed: Check veritysetup defaults if cited.

statement: dm-verity salt is prepended in format version 1 (appended in version 0); the kernel does not read the on-disk metadata header, userspace parses it and passes parameters.

dm-verity FEC (Reed-Solomon interleaved) re-validates each corrected block against its expected hash before use, so error correction can never launder corruption into a trusted read. Repaired data must be re-verified against authenticated digests.
research_needed: Test Entrybound repair/salvage paths to ensure repaired bytes are re-verified before being reported valid.

statement: UnixFS (DAG-PB, codec 0x70) multi-block files keep Links and blocksizes as equal-length sister lists so readers compute cumulative offsets and fetch only covering children; directories shard into HAMTs (fanout ~256) above 256 KiB-1 MiB.
The blocksizes sister-list is the minimal correct answer to seeking in a hash DAG and is cheaper than a full offset table.
research_needed: Compare index bytes for sizes-only vs full offset table in Entrybound's index.

statement: Git trees give content-addressed directory structure but no intra-file tree; OSTree hashes each content object with SHA-256 and can inject a composefs digest into commit metadata (ostree.composefs.v0) so a signature covers the fs-verity digest.
Sigstore/in-toto sign manifests/digests, not ranges: they answer who vouches for a root hash, not whether byte range X is consistent with it.
Practical split recommended: Merkle tree inside the archive for range verification; detached signature over the archive's root descriptor for provenance.
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound signatures bind the root descriptor (not a bare root) and that range verification needs no signature re-check per range.

statement: Design 1, flat per-chunk digest list in the index (eStargz, zstd:chunked, casync, Nydus): simplest and chosen by every container format, but the whole index must be trusted/verified first and index size is O(n).

Design 2, balanced Merkle tree with outboard encoding (Bao/Bab, fs-verity, dm-verity): O(log n) proof per range, index a fixed fraction (~0.8% at 4 KiB/SHA-256, ~3% at 1 KiB/BLAKE3); best for huge archives or memory-constrained verifiers.
Design 3, sister-list of block sizes over a hash DAG (UnixFS): O(1) offset-to-block resolution plus inherent verification, at the cost of a protobuf-shaped index.

Four ranked byte-range verification designs (flat digest list, balanced Merkle outboard, sizes sister-list DAG, hash chain to avoid) imply a format must choose one based on archive size and verifier memory.
research_needed: Measure verify-one-range cost (bytes fetched, RAM, time) for Entrybound's chosen design at 10^6-10^9 chunks.
decision_needed: Which byte-range verification structure does Entrybound use for remote partial verification, and is index trust required before any range check?

statement: Parallel compression is structurally enabled by independent frames or blocks only: pzstd, zstd -T#, pigz, pbzip2, pixz, DwarFS blocks, seekable zstd frames, EROFS pclusters all rely on it.

zstd 1.5.7 (2025-02-19) multithreading remains cautious with max 4 threads by default; 1.5.4 async I/O gave up to +45% decompression speed (I/O overlap, not parallel decode); 1.5.5 seekable speedups; 1.5.6 added ZSTD_c_targetCBlockSize.
research_needed: Pin and measure zstd version behaviour relevant to Entrybound determinism and throughput.

statement: zstd -T does not parallelise decompression; a single frame is a serial dependency chain because blocks reference the sliding window, so parallel decode needs multiple independent frames (as seekable format and pzstd output provide).
pigz compresses but does not decompress in parallel (issue #36); structural reason inferred as a single DEFLATE stream with continuous 32 KiB history; BGZF exists to remove this constraint.

location: §7 L413; What I could not verify L434
statement: Mark Adler's exact stated reasoning on pigz parallel decompression could not be retrieved; unverified.
research_needed: Read pigz issue #36 thread if cited.

statement: pixz decompresses in parallel because xz's container has genuinely independent blocks and pixz emits many plus an index: same codec family, different blocking decision changes parallelism entirely.
Independent decompression units are simultaneously the parallelism mechanism and the seek mechanism (EROFS pclusters); Git's delta depth cap is the same serial-chain constraint in delta form.
Property 1: independent compression units with no shared window/dictionary state across any boundary to be parallelised or sought to.
research_needed: Verify every Entrybound decode unit (including ChunkGroups with lookback) has a declared bounded dependency set.

statement: Escape hatch: a shared pre-loaded dictionary (WARC-zstd head dictionary frame, zstd --patch-from) keeps ratio on small units without a serial dependency.
research_needed: Measure ratio gain of shared dictionaries on small-entry corpora and dictionary fetch cost for remote access.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound support archive-level shared dictionaries, and how are they bound, versioned and budgeted?

statement: Property 2: an index of unit offsets in both compressed and decompressed coordinates; seekable zstd's 4+4-byte entry is the minimum viable form, eStargz TOC and DwarFS SECTION_INDEX elaborate forms.
research_needed: Confirm Entrybound index gives O(1)/O(log n) mapping from logical offsets to unit byte ranges.

statement: Property 3: a fixed-size, self-locating tail so a reader finds the index in one unconditional request without scanning.
research_needed: Verify Entrybound footer is fixed-size and locates the index (and descriptor) in one range read.
